generatedProse.concept-context: In practice, a sport science assignment is one connected act of critical writing. As you draw several training studies into an argument about the best way to build strength, you are already judging which evidence is more secure, and your wording carries that judgement. Weighing a controlled trial against a weaker one is synthesis, judgement and language working together, not three separate tasks.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport science students write about two training methods. One describes each study in turn, then says one looks better, but never explains why in the field's terms. The other synthesises them into an argument, judges the controlled trial more secure, and uses terms like 'progressive overload' and 'effect size' so the reasoning is clear.
generatedProse.summary: In sport science, critical writing means the three moves working as one. You synthesise several training studies into an argument, judge which evidence is more secure, and word it in the field's own terms. It is the three together that turn a set of studies into a critical argument of your own.

check.body: A student writes an essay that draws three sources into an argument, reaches a judgement about which view is stronger, and words it so each step is clear. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first programme, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next programme.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That critical writing works as one practice: the argument, the judgement and the wording all do their work in the same piece.
_items.feedback: Yes. The three moves ran together in one connected act of writing.

_items.text: That the student used too many sources for one essay.
_items.feedback: The number of sources is not the point. The three moves worked together.

_items.text: That only strong students can write this way.
_items.feedback: This is something you can practise, whatever your starting point.

_items.text: That precise wording is the only move that matters.
_items.feedback: Wording carries the judgement, but the argument and judgement matter too.
